qualifying_updates.title: Enterprise managed-settings.json becomes generally available for Copilot clients
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers can maintain a managed-settings.json file in a .github-private repository to enforce supported Copilot configuration keys across VS Code and Copilot CLI, including plugin marketplace controls, plugin enablement, bypass-permissions mode, and model selection.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Durable agent instructions and tool permissions are moving from local preference files toward centrally governed configuration. Local guidance should treat enterprise instruction and plugin policy files as part of the AI development control plane, not just editor setup.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add to governed instructions and permissions coverage: enterprise configuration precedence can override user file-based settings and should be visible during agent workflow review.

qualifying_updates.title: Enterprises can default Copilot to auto model selection
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Enterprise administrators can set the model key to auto in managed-settings.json so new Copilot conversations start with auto model selection by default, while users can still switch models per conversation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Model choice is becoming a governed default rather than a purely individual prompt-time decision. Practice guidance should separate enterprise defaults, user overrides, and task-specific model escalation criteria.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route to adoption and governance notes about model-policy ownership, override logging, and how teams decide when to pin a model instead of relying on auto.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot CLI auto model selection routes by task
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Copilot CLI auto model selection uses model availability, reliability, task dimensions such as reasoning and code-generation complexity, bug diagnosis difficulty, and tool orchestration needs to select a model. It respects admin policies and bills based on the selected model.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Model routing is being framed around task features, cache boundaries, reliability, and cost. Local model-selection guidance should account for workflow classification and cost telemetry, not only model capability rankings.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture task-based routing criteria as a practice pattern for agent orchestration and cost-aware context design.

qualifying_updates.title: AI credit session limits land in Copilot CLI and SDK public preview
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub made session limits available in public preview for Copilot CLI 1.0.66 and later and Copilot SDK 1.0.5 and later, giving users a way to cap AI credit use during a CLI or SDK session.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Long-running coding agents need explicit spend and effort guardrails at the session boundary. This supports local patterns for budgeted agent runs, stop conditions, and escalation when a task exceeds its expected cost envelope.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as evidence for session-level run budgets in agent workflow governance and operating model pages.

qualifying_updates.title: Browser tools for GitHub Copilot in VS Code reach general availability
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub Copilot browser tools in VS Code are generally available. Agents can drive a real browser, navigate live web apps, and feed findings back into chat, with user and enterprise control sections called out by the announcement.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Browser-driving agents expand verification beyond static code edits into live application inspection. Local practice notes should connect browser permissions, network-domain controls, screenshot evidence, and UI regression checks.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route to tool-call practice and verification leaves: browser access should be treated as a privileged tool surface with evidence requirements.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot vision becomes generally available
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub Copilot vision is generally available across VS Code chat, github.com Copilot Chat, and Copilot CLI. GitHub states that Business and Enterprise image and PDF attachments are retained for approximately 24 hours to provide the service.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Multimodal context ingestion adds a data-retention and evidence-handling dimension to AI-assisted development. Teams need rules for when screenshots, PDFs, architecture images, and issue attachments are appropriate inputs.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Governance pages should treat visual attachments as context artifacts with retention, sensitivity, and review boundaries.

qualifying_updates.title: Kimi K2.7 Code becomes generally available in GitHub Copilot
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Kimi K2.7 Code is now a selectable open-weight model in GitHub Copilot. It rolls out first to individual plans, with Business and Enterprise access off by default until administrators enable the policy.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Open-weight model availability inside managed coding tools raises model approval, compliance review, and task fit questions. The local wiki should route model background upstream but capture the enterprise enablement and risk-review practice.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep model facts upstream; locally capture the policy pattern: off-by-default model enablement plus security, compliance, and data-governance review before team rollout.

qualifying_updates.title: Claude Sonnet 5 becomes generally available for GitHub Copilot
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub added Claude Sonnet 5 to Copilot across IDE, CLI, cloud agent, mobile, and other surfaces, citing coding, CLI-style tasks, prompt-cache utilization, and lower-effort latency. Business and Enterprise administrators can enable access through model policy settings.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The announcement ties model selection to task surface, prompt-cache behavior, effort level, and enterprise policy. Local guidance should treat model choice as part of workflow design and not as a one-time product preference.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route broad model details upstream; locally capture the model-policy, task-surface, and prompt-cache implications for cost and reliability.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot Agent becomes available in JetBrains AI Assistant
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub and JetBrains made Copilot Agent a first-class option in JetBrains AI Assistant, including model selection and reasoning-depth controls inside AI chat. The roadmap mentions Next Edit Suggestions, Skills, and deeper orchestration across tools.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding agents are becoming IDE-native orchestration surfaces rather than standalone chat or CLI tools. Local practice should track how teams standardize handoffs, model depth, reusable skills, and review across IDEs.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as practice evidence for IDE-native agent workflows, cross-tool orchestration, and team training around agent entry points.

qualifying_updates.title: Per-user AI credit budgets become available for GitHub cost centers
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub Enterprise admins can create a per-user AI credit budget scoped to a cost center through the REST API. The budget follows cost center membership and can stop usage before the included usage pool is exhausted.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Team adoption of coding agents increasingly depends on budget shape, membership synchronization, and spend limits. Operating-model guidance should define how teams fund heavy agent users without hiding cost overruns.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route to adoption economics and governance: cost-center budgets are a concrete mechanism for team-level AI usage policy.

qualifying_updates.title: Futurum argues coding agents need an independent review layer
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Futurum describes verification, not code generation, as the emerging bottleneck for AI coding tools and argues for independent review infrastructure rather than relying on agent self-review.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This supports local guidance that separates generation agents from review/evaluation loops and treats independent verification as a workflow requirement for higher-risk code paths.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate for verification leaves covering independent review layers, review-depth rubrics, and self-review blind spots.

qualifying_updates.title: WorkOS launches a remote MCP server with audit-log operations
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: WorkOS announced a remote MCP server that can manage WorkOS account operations from AI agents, including auditing configuration, managing users, and configuring audit log streams for production environments.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Remote MCP servers are expanding from read-only context access into account administration and production-adjacent actions. Local practice should emphasize connector classification, approval requirements, audit logs, and least-privilege scopes.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record as a governed-MCP practice signal, not as a local WorkOS product page: classify admin-capable MCP tools differently from codebase retrieval tools.
